title: Why Afternoons Get Harder with Dementia (and What Helps)
description: Is Mom calm all morning, then upset by late afternoon? Here's why afternoons and evenings can get harder for someone living with dementia, and simple things that help: busy things in the morning, lamps on before sundown, quiet afternoons, a simple job, calm words, and the same bedtime routine every night.
end: You don't have to do every evening alone.

parts.head: When afternoons get hard with dementia
parts.sub: Why it happens, and what helps
parts.text: Is Mom calm all morning, then upset by four o'clock? You're not imagining it. Many families see it. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's why afternoons can get harder with dementia, and what really helps.

parts.head: By late afternoon, the brain is worn out
parts.sub: And early dark makes it harder
parts.text: By late afternoon, a brain living with dementia is worn out from a whole day of working hard to make sense of things. And in fall and winter, when it gets dark earlier, it can be even harder.

parts.head: Do the busy things in the morning
parts.sub: The bath, the errand, the walk
parts.text: So put the busy things in the morning, when they have the most energy: the bath, the errand, the doctor's visit, the walk.

parts.head: Lamps on before sundown
parts.sub: Don't let the dark sneak up
parts.text: Turn on the lamps and close the blinds before the sun goes down, so the dark doesn't sneak up on them. A bright, cozy room feels safer.

parts.head: Keep afternoons quiet and simple
parts.sub: Folding towels, soft music, the dog in her lap
parts.text: After lunch, keep things quiet and simple. Folding towels, soft music, looking through a photo album, or the dog in her lap. Turn off the loud TV.

parts.head: Give them a job
parts.text: A simple job can help, too, like snapping green beans or sorting the silverware. Everyone needs to feel useful, and that doesn't go away with dementia.

parts.head: Short, calm words. Don't argue.
parts.text: If she gets upset, use short, calm sentences, one idea at a time. Don't argue about what's real to her. Comfort her first, then gently change the subject or the room.

parts.head: The same bedtime routine, every night
parts.text: Then follow the same calm bedtime routine, in the same order, every night. Predictable routines lower worry, because there are fewer surprises to make sense of.

parts.head: Suddenly much worse? Call the doctor.
parts.sub: Pain or an infection can do that
parts.text: One important note. If evenings suddenly get much worse, call her doctor. Pain, an infection, or a medicine can cause that kind of change.

parts.head: Evenings are hard on you, too
parts.sub: Plan help for the hardest hours
parts.text: And evenings are hard on you, too. If late afternoon is the hardest time in your house, that's a good time to have help.

parts.head: Afternoon and evening visits
parts.sub: Advanced Care for dementia, and Medicare GUIDE respite
parts.text: Our caregivers can come in the afternoon and evening, keep things calm and steady, and start that bedtime routine. Our Advanced Care level is for dementia and wandering. And if your family qualifies, Medicare's GUIDE program can pay for respite visits.
Call us at (417) 234-8494, or visit mo-care.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
